nodes.summary: SET COVER is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a set-cover instance $(n, C, K)$ that is both well formed and feasible: every list in $C$ has no repeated entries and only entries less than $n$, and some sublist of $C$ with at most $K$ entries contains every natural number $y < n$ in one of its lists. Bitstrings that do not decode to…
nodes.title: The SET COVER decision problem

nodes.summary: A set-cover instance $(n, C, K)$ is feasible when there is a sublist $D$ of $C$ (a list obtained from $C$ by deleting entries while keeping their order) with at most $K$ entries such that every natural number $x < n$ belongs to some list in $D$.
nodes.title: Feasible set-cover instances

nodes.summary: A set-cover instance is a triple $(n, C, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$, the size of the universe, a finite list $C$ of finite lists of natural numbers, the subsets, and a natural number $K$, the bound.
nodes.title: Set-cover instances

nodes.summary: The SET COVER decision problem lies in NP, and every decision problem $L$ in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to SET COVER.
nodes.title: SET COVER is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A set-cover instance $(n, C, K)$ is well formed when every list $s$ in $C$ has no repeated entries and every entry of $s$ is less than $n$, that is, each member of $C$ lists the elements of a subset of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ without repetition.
nodes.title: Well-formed set-cover instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
